# MCP3008 acquisition · 0.29

Sample/hold begins on the D0 rising edge (fourth rising clock after the start bit), ends on the next clock's falling edge: 1.5 SCK periods. The null bit and B9..B0 remain in the existing SPI waveform. Acquisition uses actual AVR clock cycles, not the requested SPISettings value. Input voltages come from canonical CH/AGND/VREF nets.

The selected bounded RC approximation uses 20 pF sample capacitance and 1 kΩ internal switch resistance. Resistive source impedance is calculated by grounding the DC solution's independent sources and applying a 1 V test to the input network. Potentiometer legs, series/parallel resistors, finite output drivers and GPIO sources participate. Charging is `Vhold = Vin + (Vhold−Vin) exp(−dt/((Rsource+1000)·20pF))`, updated on acquisition clock edges. The shared held voltage persists across CS and channel changes; reset/power loss clears it. The first sample starts from 0 V. This retention/edge sampling is an explicitly selected approximation, not a fitted model of the SAR DAC's charge redistribution.

The conversion freezes at hold time; source changes afterward do not change the current conversion. Code uses floor(Vhold/VREF·1024) and 0..1023 clipping. Exactly half-scale can read 511 before full settling because quantization thresholds are discontinuous. Inspector/snapshot includes sourceOhms, acquisitionCycles, heldVoltage, acquisitionErrorLSB and timingError.

Rated endpoints: 3.6 MHz at 5 V; 1.35 MHz at 2.7 V. Between 2.7 and 5 V, this model conservatively uses 1.35 MHz; it does not interpolate a manufacturer guarantee. Below 10 kHz the model reports clock-too-slow (datasheet charge-loss warning). Above the selected maximum it reports clock-too-fast. Invalid samples shift zero; snapshot code is null and inspector INVALID. Zero outside rated timing is a deterministic simulator fallback, not a prediction of real out-of-spec hardware. A timing violation stays latched until a new CS transaction, so a delayed edge cannot erase an earlier overspeed violation. Intermediate firmware delays and instruction quantization influence the measured clock intervals.

This is a one-way Thevenin acquisition model. The internal sample capacitor is not stamped into MNA: no charge-injection current, supply/reference loading, analog pin capacitance, leakage/noise/INL/DNL, temperature dependence or electrical input protection. Capacitor/inductor/nonlinear semiconductor/opamp networks touching the source path are explicitly unsupported and yield invalid sampling rather than an ideal result. Differential pairs use the sum of each resistive leg's driving-point resistance; shared-source coupling and pseudo-differential common-mode limits are not fully modeled. Existing bit-bang transport remains supported by actual CLK edges.

New low/high source examples: 50% 10 kΩ pot through 1 kΩ / 100 kΩ, alternate grounded CH1 to charge-reset the shared hold, then CH0 at 1 MHz / 125 kHz / 4 MHz. Native firmware demonstrates 511/512/0 and 263/510/0 respectively. The 100 kΩ result improves as the acquisition window grows. Sources are real circuit resistances; environment parameters do not override the ADC result.

Source: [Microchip MCP3004/MCP3008 DS21295D, electrical specifications, Figure 4-1 and §5](https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/aemDocuments/documents/APID/ProductDocuments/DataSheets/21295d.pdf).
